limitations: No sections were missing for Aintree, so none were written.

Corner names: only a hobby blog (yorkshireferret.blogspot.com) listed names (Waterway, Anchor Crossing, Cottage, Tatt's, Melling crossing etc.) and it contains an evident error (claims a 1956 British GP at Aintree), so it is not accepted as a source. Official aintree.org.uk/history and lapledger.org carry no corner names. Wikipedia/f1-fansite were seen only as search leads. No name accepted; none could be tied to F1DB turn numbers 1-8 (F1DB 8 turns vs 10 on lapledger).

Existing prose names 'Tatts and Becher's' as coming from the racecourse; Becher's/Tatts are only seen in the blog source, so this claim in the existing narrative_biography was not independently verified.

aintree.org.uk/history credits Earl Howe and Raymond Mays in connection with the circuit's opening, while the blog credits Mirabel Topham's Aintree Automobile Racing Company (1953 formed, opened May 1954); not reconciled, so no origins text written.
